fullPassage: Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn't occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. "You're not you when you're hungry," was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word "hangry," a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work? The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control. Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies. What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry." Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry. While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks. Interestingly, the human brain's response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control. Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists' 일치

❌ ② 본문 'researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students' 일치

❌ ③ 본문 'Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment' 일치

✅ ④ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 본문 'participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand'에서 식사를 거른 참가자가 수행 능력이 '더 낮았다'고 했어요. '더 좋았다'는 정반대예요 ←정답
det.tip: skipped eating had poorer performance(거른 쪽이 더 낮음)가 사실입니다.

ch: 연구자들은 200명이 넘는 미국 대학생을 대상으로 실험을 진행했다.
참가자들은 실험 직전에 식사를 거르거나 푸짐한 식사를 하도록 요청받았다.
식사를 거른 참가자들이 미리 식사를 한 참가자들보다 수행 능력이 더 좋았다.

questions.passage: Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that "You're not you when you're hungry." Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop'와 일치 ←정답

❌ ② 본문 'When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted'에서 감정 조절 기능이 '방해받는다'고 했으므로 불일치

❌ ③ 본문 'the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills ~ are greatly altered'에서 활동이 '크게 달라진다'고 했으므로 불일치

❌ ④ 본문 'Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance'에서 감정 균형 유지에 '중요한 역할'을 한다고 했으므로 불일치
det.tip: cortisol ~ cause the serotonin level ~ to drop(코르티솔이 세로토닌을 떨어뜨림)이 일치. 나머지는 본문과 반대입니다.

ch: 높은 코르티솔 수치는 뇌의 세로토닌 수치를 떨어지게 한다.
세로토닌 수치가 불균형해져도 감정 조절 기능은 정상적으로 작동한다.
배고플 때 고차원 인지 기능을 담당하는 영역의 활동은 전혀 변하지 않는다.
신경 전달 물질은 감정의 균형을 유지하는 것과는 아무 관련이 없다.

questions.passage: In fact, scientists have ①<u>observed</u> that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when ②<u>deprived</u> of food, and schooling fish ③<u>exhibit</u> reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to ④<u>recognizing</u> them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you're just hangry. While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called "lonely hunger" works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive "emotional eating." Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ recognizing → recognize: be able to 뒤에는 동사원형
det.analysis:
① observed: 'scientists have observed that ~'에서 현재완료 have observed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② deprived: 'fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food'는 'when (they are) deprived of food'의 분사구문으로, 초파리가 먹이를 '빼앗기는' 수동이라 과거분사 deprived가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ exhibit: 'schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity'에서 주어 schooling fish(복수)에 맞는 복수 동사 exhibit가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ recognizing → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'only if they are able to ___ them'에서 'be able to + 동사원형' 구조이므로 recognize로 써야 해요. recognizing(동명사/분사)은 to 뒤에 올 수 없어 틀려요. ❌ recognizing은 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: be able to + 동사원형: able to recognize

questions.passage: It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies. What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 인체가 배고픔이라는 위협에 대응하기 위해 분비하는, 스트레스 상황에 대처하도록 돕는 호르몬은 무엇인지 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations.'에서 인체가 위협에 대응하여 분비하는, 스트레스 상황 대처를 돕는 호르몬은 cortisol(코르티솔)이다.
det.tip: releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations에서 cortisol을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 신체적 영양 부족이 심리적 불편함으로 이어지듯, 사회적 영양의 부족이 낳는다고 한 감정을 본문에서 찾아 두 단어로 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger'에서 신체적 영양 부족이 심리적 불편함으로 이어지듯, 사회적 영양의 부족은 'social hunger(사회적 허기)'라는 감정을 낳는다고 했다.
det.tip: a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger에서 social hunger를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by __________ (release) cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'responds to this threat by ___ cortisol'에서 빈칸은 전치사 by의 목적어 자리다. 전치사 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 하므로 release를 releasing으로 바꿔야 한다. 'by releasing cortisol(코르티솔을 분비함으로써)'로 해석된다.

questions.passage: Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny? After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed.

questions.passage: Studies also support the notion that __________, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"외로움은 배고픔과 비슷한 신호로 작용한다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, as, hunger, loneliness, serves, signal, similar, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger
det.analysis:
주어는 loneliness(외로움), 동사는 serve as(~로서 작용하다)인데 주어가 3인칭 단수이므로 serves가 돼요: loneliness + serves + as.

무엇으로 작용하는가 하면 '하나의 신호'예요: a + signal.

'배고픔과 비슷한'은 형용사 similar + to로 신호를 꾸며요: similar + to + hunger.

순서대로 이으면 loneliness / serves / as / a / signal / similar / to / hunger.
det.tip: serve as(~로서 작용하다) + similar to(~와 비슷한): 단수 주어라 serves
